audit_B: independent external Kalshi market-data audit (kx/* data not in this repository; claims as relayed)
rule: Conflicting numbers stay side by side; nothing is averaged. A status names which measurement is wrong or whether the two measure different populations.

claims.claim: Average entry ask of the paper book
claims.audit_A: 79.72¢ over all 190 fills (82.16¢ over the 137 policy-era one-contract HOLD fills)
claims.population_B: net + count arithmetic assuming a flat 1¢ fee, 149 'wins' (positive-net rows) and HOLD identity on 24 exit-priced A0 rows
claims.resolution: An implied ask cannot be recovered from a headline that pools exit-priced legacy rows; the stored ask is the record.

claims.claim: Win count
claims.audit_A: 140 official settlement wins / 190 (117 / 137 policy era)
claims.population_B: stored_pnl_cents > 0 (9 legacy early exits closed positive without settling in the money)
claims.evidence: ledger CSV columns official_win vs stored_pnl_cents
claims.resolution: A positive-net exit is not a win (METRIC_CONTRACT.md).

claims.claim: Live and shadow fills are commingled in the book
claims.audit_A: No: live (entry_cents/ev_cents) and shadow (shadow_entry_cents/shadow_ev_cents) are separate columns; never summed
claims.population_B: the all-time headline (+92) which pools 24 A0 legacy exit rows and 3 scratches with 166 HOLD rows
claims.evidence: ledger CSV ledger_tag/hold_identity; books.server.ts all-time scope
claims.resolution: What B saw is legacy-exit pooling in one headline scope, not live/shadow commingling.

claims.claim: Taker fee is 1¢ at every price
claims.audit_A: ceil(7·p·(1−p)) per order: 2¢ from 18¢ to 82¢, 1¢ from 83¢ to 99¢ (C=1); at C=100 the order pays 0.52–1.75¢ per contract
claims.population_A: fee-engine KALSHI_TAKER_7PCT_CEIL_CENT_V1 (VENUE_TABLE_VERIFIED_2026_07_07; official schedule effective 2026-07-07; KXBTC15M absent from non-standard series table)
claims.population_B: unstated contract count (consistent with C≥50 at 80–90¢)
claims.resolution: For the one-contract paper book B's fee understates cost by 1¢ on every whole-cent fill from 18¢ through 82¢. The official Kalshi schedule effective 2026-07-07 verifies the charged engine's published one-contract table and default M=1 for KXBTC15M; sub-cent centicent treatment remains separately ASSUMED.

claims.claim: Kalshi quotes carry 0.1¢ ticks
claims.audit_A: Yes below 10¢ and at/above 90¢ (desk_lag_events raw book); the desk coerces to whole cents before booking
claims.resolution: 28 historical fills at ≥90¢ have an exact ask UNKNOWN to ±0.5¢; no fill between 10¢ and 90¢ is affected.

claims.claim: Settlement strike is the prior window's official settlement value
claims.audit_A: Yes on 1,337 of 1,357 windows with a prior ledger row; 9 windows carry the desk's $25-grid proxy strike (round(spot/25)*25, live.ts); 11 early-era windows (2026-09-07→10) mismatch by −$314..+$104, cause UNKNOWN; ties never observed (0 rows)
claims.resolution: The 9 proxy-grid windows are listed in docs/SETTLEMENT_SEMANTICS_2026-09-22.md; whether the official strike differed on them is UNKNOWN; every winner still comes from kalshi-result.

claims.claim: The 80¢ floor trial beat the 70¢ shadow by +215¢ over 442 windows
claims.audit_A: +215 = A(−415 on 91 shared fills: −426 price, +11 fee) + B(+630: 11 losing 70¢-only fills avoided) + C(0) + D(0)
claims.population_A: desk_ledger trial rows 2026-09-10T23:00Z–2026-09-15T14:05Z (442 windows; 440 with replay)
claims.resolution: The arithmetic is confirmed; the interpretation splits: the higher floor cost 415¢ on the shared fills and saved 630¢ by not taking 11 fills that lost.

claims.claim: The Chair (selector) adds nothing beyond a price floor
claims.audit_A: On the 440 trial windows: live Chair +2.25¢/fill (n=91, WR 87.9) vs blind-80 first touch +0.59¢/fill (n=374) vs matched controls +1.05¢/fill (WR 85.3, n=8,801 pooled)
claims.population_A: MARKET_BASELINE first-touch rules on desk_replay 4 s paths
claims.resolution: Direction favours the selector; 91 fills cannot separate +2.25 from +1.05 (WR 87.9 vs 85.3, Wilson LB 79.6). Not resolvable from this sample.

claims.claim: A blind 80¢ first-touch buyer loses in both halves
claims.resolution: Confirmed on internal data; the counts differ (1,362 vs 1,440) so the populations are not identical.

claims.claim: MIRROR-35 (buy the 30–45¢ side, T−5..T−2) earns +1.89¢/fill
claims.audit_A: TRAIN +1.89¢/fill (n=293) → TEST −0.60 (n=299); ALL +0.63; ~60 cells searched
claims.resolution: The train figure reproduces exactly and the sign flips out of sample; discovery-biased. Registered CANDIDATE_NOT_COLLECTING.

claims.claim: Jump-chase (≥2¢ rise in 60 s) is profitable
claims.audit_A: TRAIN +0.13¢/fill → TEST −1.91
claims.resolution: Sign flips; not a candidate.

claims.claim: Late 95–99¢ buying loses
claims.resolution: Confirmed both halves.

claims.claim: The Chair's WAIT rate is inflated by chalk (≥99¢) windows
claims.resolution: Chalk moves the WAIT rate by under one point at every checkpoint. Both denominators are kept.

claims.claim: 1,440-window sample
claims.audit_A: 1,362 windows with replay paths (1,176 complete) in the bound
claims.resolution: The external sample is not reproducible here; nothing was tuned to either count.

claims.claim: The seat review is a one-way ratchet
claims.audit_A: Yes: every seat with 8+ legs sits under the 15¢ floor; each review that fires demotes; AUTO_SKILL_PROMOTION_ENABLED=false returns nothing to LIVE
claims.resolution: Next reviews by calls-until: PULSE 71 (no LIVE card to bench; debt reset + rethink spawn), TAPE 127, CHAIN 223, INDEX 273 (would bench INDEX.settle_fair, its lower-EV LIVE card), DRIFT 403 (would bench DRIFT.aligned_3h), CASCADE 406, STREAK 497, WHALE 497, STRIKE 499.

claims.claim: A two-seat quorum is reachable
claims.audit_A: In 2,069 seat-read ticks (2026-09-21T17:06Z–23:59Z) only DRIFT (334) and INDEX (12) were ever raw-directional, never on the same tick
claims.resolution: Unreachable on every tick of that population; UNKNOWN before 2026-09-21T17:06Z (no seat reads).

claims.claim: A 92¢ cap would help
claims.audit_A: 15 policy-era fills at ≥92¢, all won, +75¢; cap would have cost 75¢ in-sample (Wilson LB 79.6% vs need 95.0%)
claims.resolution: No historical support for the cap; no proof of edge above 92¢ either. Telemetry only; not adopted.

claims.claim: A price-aware edge gate beats the flat 3¢ gate
claims.audit_A: Model edge at entry is not stored (UNKNOWN). On the 89 fills with a settlement-index estimate: no gate +276 (n=89); FLAT_3C proxy +111 (54); QUARTER_OF_WIN +122 (53); FEE_PLUS_2 +59 (51); oracle ceiling +1105
claims.resolution: Every gate variant removed more winners than losers on this sample; evaluation only, nothing changed.

claims.claim: 17/17 and 19/19 records prove card edge
claims.audit_A: 17/17: Wilson LB 81.6% vs need 90.5% at 89.5¢; 19/19: 83.2% vs 84.0% at 82¢ → PROMISING_INSUFFICIENT
claims.resolution: Neither lower bound clears the need. Card-level booked asks are UNKNOWN; the table uses the quoted asks.
